subject: Retention addendum + erase scheduler for ArcadiaHealth
messages:
From: Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops_lead@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2028-09-11T08:14:00Z
Subject: Request: retention addendum & deletion scheduling

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking a look at this. Arcadia is updating its clinical investigation procedures and we need a short-term retention carveout to support investigations that may be opened up to ~90 days after an event. Specifically: 

- We need a temporary hold that prevents backups from being purged for up to 90 days for a tagged patient cohort.
- We also need a predictable, auditable erase schedule for non-tagged data (so our auditors can reconcile deletions).
- Please provide the full subprocessor list for backups and the countries where snapshots/archives may be stored.

I've attached a draft DPA addendum (DPA_addendum_draft_v2.pdf) with our suggested wording and a short SOW note.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) implement a per-account "retention window override" that can be applied to tagged datasets, and
2) provide an immutable snapshot for 45 days as a fallback?

We appreciate a timeline for when Redwood can ship the change, and whether there are any audit or cost implications.

Best,
Emily Torres
Director, Cloud Ops
ArcadiaHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-11T12:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: retention addendum & deletion scheduling

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. I've skimmed the addendum and included Karthik + Kim for legal and product-level constraints; Marcus will scope ops impact. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, we can add a tenant-level "retention override" flag tied to a tag. It will be an opt-in configuration we can expose in the Console and via API.
- Immutable snapshots for 45 days are possible via a short-lived immutable S3/GCS lifecycle + retention marker; there are cost and throughput implications we should surface.

Proposal for timeline and schedule (high level):
- Week 0–2: product spec + DPA redline (we'll produce a tracked version).
- Week 3–4: ops implementation: add retention-override metadata, staging rollout to Dedicated tenants.
- Week 5: small canary with Arcadia (non-prod) and acceptance test for purge and snapshot immutability.
- Week 6: production rollout and runbook handoff.

Operational default I'd propose:
- Active snapshots: immediate point-in-time snapshot on write.
- Tagged cohort hold: backups retained but immutable snapshots only for first 45 days; full backup purge deferral up to 90 days (automated flag to release hold after 90d).
- Non-tagged: backup purge at 30 days by default, with logs retained 180 days (can carve out longer for support logs).

I'll attach a CSV with a suggested schedule (backup_schedule.csv) showing the proposed windows — take a look and let us know which pieces are negotiable.

Two clarifying Qs for your legal team:
1) Do you require a hard contractual guarantee for the 90-day hold, or is a documented runbook and audit trail sufficient?
2) Any preferred regional restriction for archived snapshots (US-only vs permitted cross-border)?

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-12T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: retention addendum & deletion scheduling

Emily / team — tagging a few legal points and a redline request from our side. I'm including the highlights here; we'll upload a tracked redline of the PDF shortly.

- Subprocessors: we'll provide an up-to-date subprocessor matrix including storage, backups, and any cloud infra partners. We need to confirm whether Arcadia requires subprocessor-specific SLA amendments.
- Cross-border: if Arcadia requires US-only storage, there will be an operational constraint for some of our backup replication lanes — we'll note the regions and propose a geo-fenced option (additional charges apply).
- Contractual guarantee: a guaranteed 90-day immutable hold is fine if limited to tagged cohorts and subject to the exception runbook (e.g., in a lawful request we may need to export / hand off data).
- Evidence: Arcadia asked for auditability — we'll provide deletion proof (time-stamped purge logs) and a retention/handoff runbook as part of the addendum.

Open item for discussion: emergency purge freeze requests (for investigations). Do you want a manual on-call approval flow from Arcadia to pause scheduled purges, or should we implement an API-driven "forensic hold" toggle?

On the DocuSign front, we can prepare an addendum once redlines are resolved.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: ArcadiaHealth Legal <legal@arcadiahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: 2028-09-13T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: retention addendum & deletion scheduling

Hannah / Karthik — thanks for the quick responses. A few counterpoints from our compliance team after reviewing the proposal: 

- We prefer a contractual guarantee for the 90-day retention hold on tagged cohorts. Operational toggles are fine for non-contractual items, but the hold needs to be binding for audit purposes.
- Emergency forensic hold: we require both an API-driven toggle and a secondary manual approval (email-confirmed from our security@arcadiahealth.com alias) so there is dual control.
- Immutable snapshot: 45 days is acceptable if it is demonstrably immutable (we need a short description of how immutability is enforced and the storage provider used).
- Subprocessor list: please include the backup vendor's name, their subprocessors, and the countries where data may transit or be persisted.

Attached: high-level runbook expectations (we referenced in-line in the PDF).

If you can provide a tracked redline and a one-page technical note describing snapshot immutability and purge proof generation, we'll route to procurement for an expedited sign-off.

Regards,
ArcadiaHealth Legal

On Thu, Sep 11, 2028 at 08:14 Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily.torres@arcadiahealth.com>, ArcadiaHealth Legal <legal@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-15T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention addendum + erase scheduler for ArcadiaHealth (next steps)

Emily / Legal — summary & next steps below. We appreciate the specifics; here's what we'll deliver this week and a proposed go/no-go timeline for pilot.

What Redwood will deliver (by 2028-09-22):
- Tracked redline of the DPA addendum that includes a bounded contractual 90-day retention hold for tagged cohorts (per Arcadia request).
- One-page technical note describing immutability (object lock + WORM lifecycle + provider identities) and locations.
- Full subprocessor matrix with regions and backup vendor subprocessors.
- A short runbook for emergency forensic hold that supports an API toggle + email-confirmed manual approval flow.
- Updated backup_schedule.csv with the proposed staged purge windows (45d immutable snapshot, 90d hold for tagged cohorts, default 30d purge for non-tagged, 180d log retention for support logs).

Operational details / caveats:
- Geo-fence option is feasible but will require separate provisioning; approximate lead time: 4–6 weeks for dedicated replication lanes.
- If Arcadia requires immutable snapshots beyond 45d, we will need to model cost impact and incorporate into the SOW.

Proposed pilot timeline:
- 9/22: deliver materials + redline.
- 9/25: sync call to finalize legal language (30 min).
- 10/2: non-prod canary (Arcadia to provide test dataset and sign-off criteria).
- 10/9: target production rollout if canary passes.

Action items assigned:
- Hannah: deliver redline & tech note (in-drive link).
- Karthik: prepare subprocessor matrix & prepare final contract language.
- Marcus: scope ops provisioning for geo-fence and estimate costs.
- Emily: confirm whether procurement requires the dual-control flow documented in the SOW.

Thanks — we'll follow up with the redline and a DocuSign link once legal agrees. If you want a call tomorrow to speed things up, I can make time.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
